title: drawspec document, version 1
description: A declarative diagram. The author describes what the diagram means; every decision that requires seeing the output — coordinates, type size, colour, arrow-head geometry, z-order — is taken by drawspec and has no field here. Referential rules (node ids are unique; an edge names nodes that exist) are beyond JSON Schema and are enforced by `drawspec validate`.

$schema.description: Optional, and only for editors: the URL of this schema.

caption.description: A line of text belonging to the whole diagram rather than to any one element — an axis's units, a condition that holds throughout, the sentence the original wrote alongside the figure. Drawn outside the drawing; the theme's `[canvas] caption` says above or below. Use a `note` for something attached to one element.

width.description: Overrides the theme's canvas width. Binding.

height_binding.description: Makes height a constraint rather than a hint.

theme.description: A bundled theme name or the path of a theme file.

nodes.description: The boxes. Order is not a coordinate — the layout decides where a box goes — but it is the order siblings are drawn in: where nothing else separates two boxes of the same rank, they read in the order written here.

edges.description: What connects to what. A `tree` takes one edge per child.

groups.description: Boxes drawn around sets of nodes, each with its own caption.

bands.description: Named things that run alongside a set of boxes rather than containing them — drawn as a labelled bar beside the boxes they accompany. For the activity that goes on throughout: a source sheet with one continuous concern above its steps and another below says the steps are *surrounded* by them, and two such bands are peers. A `group` cannot say that — a box sits inside one container or none, so two groups over the same members had to be nested, which draws a hierarchy that is not there.

columns.description: Column headings, left to right. Omit for a matrix with none.

edges.description: What connects to what, between cells that carry an `id`. The cells of a grid are not always only cells: one may produce another, or come before it. The grid places them; the relations are a separate thing, and without them a reader sees a table where the source drew a process.

key.description: What each group of cells is called, for the key drawn under the grid. Without one, a group is announced to the reader under the name the cells use for it — which is fine when that name is a name, and is how an id-shaped key like `carrega` ends up as visible text.

spans.description: Named distances between two waypoints, drawn as a capped line with the name beside it. For the quantity that is the gap itself: a cost variance is not a point on the drawing, it is how far one curve is from another, and a caption saying so states it without showing it. Either way round — two waypoints at one moment measure vertically, two at one value measure along.

axes.description: Both axes. A named shape still needs saying what it is a shape of.

curves.description: The shapes drawn, each through its own waypoints.

label.description: Required: an unlabelled axis cannot be read.

unit.description: What the numbers are in, written after the label.

min.description: Where the axis starts. Omit to take it from the data.

max.description: Where the axis ends. Omit to take it from the data.

categories.description: Names for the positions 1, 2, 3 … along this axis, instead of numbers. What a bar chart's horizontal axis usually is: the quarters, the service models, the teams.

text.description: The words themselves. May carry inline spans — `code` for the monospace role and **bold** for emphasis — because those are semantic, not typographic. A newline says this label is a lead and a detail rather than one sentence; the theme's `[box] lead` decides what the first paragraph looks like. Prefer it to punctuating the two apart inside one line.

members.description: The ids of the nodes this band accompanies. Unlike a group's, they are a set rather than a container: a band names something that runs alongside those boxes, and the same box may be under any number of bands.

id.description: Optional, and only needed to join this cell to another: an edge names the two cells it runs between. Unique within the document.

text.description: The words themselves. May carry inline spans — `code` for the monospace role and **bold** for emphasis — because those are semantic, not typographic. A newline says this label is a lead and a detail rather than one sentence; the theme's `[box] lead` decides what the first paragraph looks like. Prefer it to punctuating the two apart inside one line.

column.description: Which column this cell starts in, counting from zero.

row.description: Which row it starts in, from zero.

across.description: How many columns it covers. Default 1.

down.description: How many rows it covers. Default 1.

group.description: Which group this cell belongs to. Cells sharing a group are filled alike; the theme decides how. Naming the fill itself is not an author's decision.

role.description: The semantic role, which the theme resolves to an appearance. Defaults to 'step'.

name.description: Drawn where the curve ends. Omit it when there is only one curve and the axes already say what it is.

waypoints.description: The points the curve passes through, in order. Two is a line.

role.description: The semantic role, which the theme resolves to an appearance. Defaults to 'step'.

from.description: The id of the source node — or, in a graph kind, of a group: an edge may name a container, for a relation that belongs to the whole of it rather than to any one box inside. It may not join a container to something already within it.

to.description: The id of the target node — or, in a graph kind, of a group. The same id space as `from`.

label.description: A short label placed along the edge.

role.description: The semantic role, which the theme resolves to an appearance. Defaults to 'flow'.
